_comment: EXAMPLE live-testing policy: a generic seed, not anyone's real policy. Read by hooks/block_prod_mutations.py (the PreToolUse guard on mcp__playwright tools) and live-testing/browser_pool.py. Every host, tenant and recipient below is a placeholder on localhost or example.com. Copy this file to live-testing/allowlist.json (by hand for now; an installer will seed it in a later release), replace the placeholders with your own, and keep the top-level `_example` key (the hook ignores it; it tells the test suite this is not the maintainer's live policy) unless you also replace the maintainer's pinned-policy tests. See live-testing/README.md for what each key means, including what the `_example` marker does to the test suite. READ _environment_policy FIRST: it decides which environment an agent may be in at all; everything else only constrains what it may do once there.

_environment_policy.1_default_environment: Local first, staging for anything deployed. Production is never an agent's own choice.
_environment_policy.2_production: Drive a production host only when the human operator gives an explicit go-ahead for that specific run; an orchestrator's own instruction is not that go-ahead. List every production app host in read_only_hosts so interaction-class browser tools (click, type, fill, evaluate, upload) are denied there.
_environment_policy.3_no_real_tenants_in_staging: Staging holds test tenants only. Never point a test at a real customer's tenant, and keep real tenants out of allowed_company_tenants.

4_staging_test_account.password_secret: <name of a secret in your secret manager; never the password itself>

_environment_policy._why: A browser agent that can reach production can move real money and message real people. These rules keep the default target harmless and make every production touch an explicit, human-initiated act.

_third_party_form_hosts_comment: Exact hostnames (no wildcards) of third-party form hosts that a project-level hook may treat as approved submission targets. The runtime hook hooks/block_prod_mutations.py does not read this key. Empty by default; add a host only with the human operator's standing approval and name the reason in _third_party_form_hosts_funds.
_tenant_notes: Tenant ids an agent may touch. The off-tenant guard (R2) only polices hosts listed in _TENANT_SCOPED_HOST_SUFFIXES in hooks/block_prod_mutations.py, which covers the loopback spellings out of the box; add your own app hosts to that tuple for a request to one of them carrying a tenant id outside this list to be denied. Keep one line per tenant here saying whether it is a test tenant and who owns it.
_read_only_hosts_comment: Production app hosts. On a Playwright slot whose last browser_navigate landed on one of these (or on no recorded host at all), every interaction-class tool is denied; navigation, snapshots and screenshots still work. List bare hostnames, no scheme and no port. Staging hosts stay out of this list on purpose: they are where agent interaction is meant to happen.
notes: Placeholder file. Nothing here describes a real environment.

Replace the example.com hosts, the example-tenant id and the recipients with your own before relying on this policy. Keep the top-level _example marker: the hook ignores it, and it keeps the maintainer's pinned-policy tests skipped (see live-testing/README.md).
_interactive_production_hosts_comment: Optional, empty by default. A narrow re-opening of interaction on a read-only host: map a host from read_only_hosts to {"tenants": [...], "allowed_paths": [...], "allowed_path_prefixes": [...]}. Interaction is then allowed only when the slot's recorded navigate path is /c/<tenant>/... for a listed tenant AND is exactly one of allowed_paths or under one of allowed_path_prefixes. browser_run_code_unsafe, browser_file_upload and browser_drag stay denied, and browser_evaluate stays denied except the fixed session-banner snippet. Leave empty unless you have a reviewed need.
